- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to avoid underestimating upward momentum.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5) and price is trending down, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast slope to avoid premature bottoming.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots — cap forecast growth to 5–7% per period to avoid overbought bias.  
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often lags — adjust forecast upward by 1–2 points in the 3rd–5th period of the 30-day window.  
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome by 2–3% over 3–5 periods, apply mean reversion bias — add 0.5–1.0% to forecast in next period if sentiment remains neutral or mildly positive.  
- If sentiment is flat (±0.1–0.3) and price is trending, model often fails to capture momentum — increase forecast slope by 0.1–0.3% per period to align with implied volatility.
